sections.h2: Where Ocala owners take tax questions
sections.html:
Ocala sits in Marion County, so the county appraiser sets its values and the county collector mails the bills. Millage comes from several boards, including the City of Ocala, the county commission and the school board.

You can visit the appraiser at 501 SE 25th Avenue in Ocala, with or without an appointment. Online, the office runs a homestead e-file, a tax estimator and a mortgage estimate letter, and links out to the TRIM notice and the value adjustment board.

Another Marion County exists in Texas with its own tax office, so double-check that you are searching the Florida county.

The city had 71,753 residents in 2025, a gain of 12.7 percent over 2020, spread over 47.26 square miles. The median owner-occupied value is $241,400 and median gross rent is $1,359. Only 52.1 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so rental parcels are common. Rented homes cannot hold a homestead exemption, so a landlord selling an Ocala rental should expect the buyer's bill to follow the non-homestead rules.

Owner costs run $1,598 a month with a mortgage and $573 without one, a gap worth showing a first-time buyer.

sections.h2: How a tax bill is built
sections.html:
The appraiser multiplies value after exemptions by the millage the taxing bodies set, then certifies the roll for collection. Dates below follow the state schedule.

Ocala property tax calendar
DateWhat happens
January 1Value is set
March 1Exemption applications close
AugustTRIM notice mails; 25 days to petition on value, 30 days to contest a denied exemption
NovemberBills mail; 4 percent discount
March 31Deferral applications due with Form DR-570
April 1Unpaid bills turn delinquent

Buyers can try the appraiser's estimator for a rough figure. Their value restarts after the sale, so your old bill is a poor guide.

You can handle most paperwork from home. The appraiser's website points to these tools:

  • Property search, a map tool and a sales search for checking what nearby parcels went for.
  • A homestead exemption e-file and a property tax estimator.
  • A mortgage estimate letter, which lenders and buyers sometimes request.
  • A mailing address change form, handy if you move out ahead of closing.
  • A form to report property damage, and a separate link to report homestead fraud.
  • Pages for tangible personal property: an e-filed return, an extension request and forms.

Before you list an Ocala home, run the sales search for your street and print the results. Nearby sales answer the buyer who asks why your price differs from the assessed value. The office also posts important dates, a taxpayer's bill of rights and frequently asked questions.

Many Ocala sellers are investors or heirs, not homestead owners. A non-homestead parcel is limited to 10 percent growth a year, and that limit ends at sale.

Heirs have extra steps. A personal representative's deed under a probated will carries no stamp tax, but estate planning transfers get no blanket exemption. Florida requires no estate tax return for deaths after 2004.

  • Summary administration fits a non-exempt estate of $150,000 or less, or a death more than two years back.

Limited-income seniors may defer part of a homestead bill, so ask the collector how a deferral plays out in a sale before you take an offer.

Open the parcel record on the appraiser's site and read the owner name, mailing address and exemptions. A wrong name or address delays notices, and an exemption still on a house you rented out will raise questions with the buyer's lender.

Then ask the collector to confirm every year is paid. Bills follow the calendar year, so a summer sale has no mailed bill yet and the title company estimates it. A house once rented furnished may owe tangible personal property tax on the furniture and equipment, with a return due by April 1.

  • Ask the title company for a tax proration worksheet early.
  • Gather any denial letters or value notices still in dispute.
  • Tell the buyer which taxing bodies appear on the bill, including the City of Ocala.

November payments get 4 percent off, followed by 3, 2 and 1 percent through February. Even if no bill arrives, the owner has to find the amount and pay before April 1.

If paying in one lump is hard, ask the collector about installments (apply by May 1) or a partial payment before delinquency. Seniors with limited income can use Form DR-570 by March 31 to defer part of a homestead bill.

To qualify for the exemption of up to $50,000, the house must be your permanent residence on January 1, and the application is due March 1. Yearly growth in assessed value was capped at 2.7 percent for 2026.

A sale resets the next assessment to just value, with exceptions for spouse transfers and certain transfers on death. An owner buying again in Florida can ask the appraiser about carrying savings to the new home through portability.

These are general steps any seller can take. Print your parcel record and last tax statement. Write down who holds any mortgage and request a payoff letter. List every exemption you have on file so you can tell the buyer and the title agent what will drop off. Keep the dates of any notice you receive, and note which deadline each one starts. Finally, decide who in your household will sign documents and make sure that person's name matches the deed exactly.

Doing this before the first showing means a contract can move quickly, and it gives you a clear answer when a buyer asks about taxes.

sections.h2: What happens at an Ocala closing
sections.html:
At the table, the title company confirms payoffs, splits the current year's tax between you and the buyer, and has you sign the deed, which the clerk then records. Ask for the settlement statement a day early so any tax line you cannot place can be explained.

With cash there is no lender appraisal or underwriting, so the calendar shortens. Tax and title chores are unchanged: leftover balances come out of your proceeds and recorded liens get released before title passes.

sections.h2: Deed taxes, fees and back taxes
sections.html:
A deed for an Ocala property is taxed at the statewide 70 cents per $100 of consideration (section 201.02). Everyone on the deed stays liable, and the clerk takes payment. Clerk recording charges start at $5.00 for the first page (section 28.24).

  • Warranty, special warranty and quit claim deeds are taxable.
  • Certain spousal and divorce deeds for the marital home are exempt.

Back taxes lead to certificates sold by June 1 and, later, a possible deed sale. Settle the account with the collector before listing, and have the title company pull a payoff so closing figures are firm.

faqs.q: Which county taxes a home in Ocala?
faqs.a: Marion County, Florida. The county's appraiser values the home and its collector bills it, using millage from several bodies that includes the City of Ocala.

faqs.q: What is Ocala's median home value?
faqs.a: $241,400. Median rent is $1,359, and 52.1 percent of units have owners living in them.

faqs.q: Where can an Ocala owner visit the appraiser?
faqs.a: At 501 SE 25th Avenue in Ocala. Walk-ins and appointments are both welcome, and the phone number is (352) 368-8300.

faqs.q: Can an Ocala rental property have homestead?
faqs.a: No. Homestead is lost if the unit is rented, so a rental is assessed without the exemption and the owner's cap does not transfer to a buyer.

faqs.q: Is the Ocala tax bill reset when the house sells?
faqs.a: Yes. A transfer of title sends the next assessment to just value, so a buyer cannot count on the seller's bill.
